inputCaptureQuality.scope: Lag uses WS display ticks and local callback ticks. Pixel gaps may reflect unchanged content; neither gap series proves lossless capture. Signed clock anomalies are preserved.

sourceInputProof.scope: Explicitly supplied source JSON only; no automatic same-session guarantee or host/guest clock subtraction. Full-source draw rate is not the fixed host video-window delivered rate. Unknown source fields are not exported.

video.sourceAnchor: Host input-helper-call-before for V (includes foreground check/event creation/post); not guest callback time.

sampleClassification.definition: mixed: at least two valid required-region codes differ, even if other regions are unread. undecodable: not all424 coherent and fewer than two distinct valid codes. Eight documented pointer regions are excluded from every test.

timeWeightedOccupancy.assumption: Latest decoded state is held until the next non-Idle event, clipped to capture start/end and the fixed analysis window. Mixed/undecodable intervals are not called a held old frame. This is sampled-state occupancy, not continuous proof.

video.noNewCoherentIdGapScope: Includes [T0,first change] and [last change,T1]. These are gaps in consistent-ID progress, not proof that all pixels froze; mixed/unknown may still change.

regionUpdates.scope: Each required region's distinct CRC-validated VIDEO IDs / fixed45s, independent of all424 coherence. This is region update rate, never complete FPS. Spans are max-min numeric16-bit IDs among valid regions in the same raw pixel sample; no source/client drop attribution and no wrap correction.

captureQualityInWindow.scope: Lag uses WS display ticks and local callback ticks. Pixel gaps may reflect unchanged content; neither gap series proves lossless capture. Signed clock anomalies are preserved.

limits: Observed distinct all424 VIDEO IDs divided by the predeclared 45 seconds; not callback FPS or native complete-frame instrumentation.
The second ID rate removes IDs already seen before the window; main unique-ID rate can include one held boundary ID.
Sampling can miss short coherent states. Unseen IDs are not assigned to guest, server, network, client or capture drops.
Grid consistency is an operational sampled definition, not proof every natural-color pixel or physical scanout is atomic.
Incomplete recordings retain the fixed denominator but are flagged invalid for a whole-window comparison; unrecorded occupancy is unobserved, not fabricated stale content.

sourceVideo.scope: Explicitly supplied source JSON only; no automatic same-session guarantee or host/guest clock subtraction. Full-source draw rate is not the fixed host video-window delivered rate. Unknown source fields are not exported.

captureChildWholeRunCost.scope: wait4 capture-child resource usage; includes setup, calibration, 81-second capture and evidence writes; not client CPU.

limits: Single Mac and fixed coded synthetic workload; not a general/native-video performance ranking.
Latency starts before the input helper, which includes foreground check/event creation/CGEventPost; before/after brackets retained. Endpoint is WindowServer displayTime, not panel photons.
100 samples per input kind per primary client; empirical tail quantiles are not stable population estimates. Additional Maspice run shows a 480ms maximum.
424 required region codes of432, with eight documented pointer exclusions. Sampling may miss brief coherent states; output is not exact client drop rate.
Capture adds measurable overhead; wait4 whole-run child CPU is about14% of one core. Actual sample cadence and lag are recorded; requested120Hz is not a guarantee.
Cocoa dynamic code fields fail in three quarters even at2048 resolution; do not interpret raw0 consistent states or0 validated mixed samples as0FPS or no tearing.
Previous gradient CPU measurements are a different workload and capture setup; no CPU-to-speed conversion.
No client/renderer/server product code was changed; unique vertical-phase root cause remains unresolved.
